 Nuggets Notes: S. Jones, Jokic, Supporting Cast, Hopkins
 By Rory Maher |
 at November 6, 2026 9:44 pm 
 Nuggets forward Spencer Jones isn’t on the injury report ahead of Saturday’s game against Indiana in Mexico City, tweets Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette, which means the former Stanford Cardinal is set to make his season debut.
 Jones and the team had been targeting Saturday for his 2026/27 debut throughout this week, a source tells Bennett Durando of The Denver Post ( Twitter link ).
 After playing a modest role as a rookie, Jones emerged as an important rotation player for the Nuggets last season amid a wave of injuries at forward. He was converted from a two-way to a standard contract in February after he reached his active-game limit, and then signed a two-year, $11.75MM offer sheet with the Thunder as a restricted free agent this summer, a deal the Nuggets matched .
 Jones, who dealt with hamstring issues last season,  tweaked his hamstring during training camp at the beginning of October and subsequently underwent an MRI, which revealed a strain. He said before the regular season that he expected to play in the opener, but he has been held out of Denver’s first seven games with what the team called bilateral hamstring injury management.
 Veteran forward DeMar DeRozan is probable to play Saturday after missing Wednesday’s contest due to back spasms, per Benedetto.
 Here’s more on the Nuggets:
 Denver needs much more from both Nikola Jokic and his supporting cast if the team hopes to make any kind of playoff run this season, according to Ben Golliver of ESPN.com . As Golliver writes, the three-time MVP has gotten off to a slow start this fall, notably calling out fans for booing when the team played poorly in the first half of the home opener. The Nuggets are 4-3, but have an 0-3 record against winning teams, Golliver notes, and the talent drain they’ve endured since their 2023 title has been obvious early on this season with Jokic not playing at his typical level. Aaron Gordon and Cameron Johnson also haven’t been sharp to open 2026/27, Golliver adds, and the bench has largely struggled as well. Giving Jokic a massive long-term contract next summer is looking like an increasingly risky proposition for the Nuggets, given that they’re already the only team operating over the second tax apron and there’s no recent precedent for a big man to continue to playing at an MVP level through his age-36 season (that would be the fifth year of a theoretical new deal), per Golliver.
 Jokic looked more like his usual self in Wednesday’s win over Toronto, according to Durando of The Denver Post , having recorded 32 points (on 13-of-19 shooting), 11 assists, 10 rebounds and three steals in 30 minutes in a dominant victory in which he sat for the entire fourth quarter. Crucially, Jokic was able to operate in the post, with the Nuggets struggling to get him the ball down low in previous games. “ I think a lot of it’s been the pressure, ” head coach David Adelman said. “ We’ve had to initiate offense earlier, which leads to him at the top of the key, which is a lot more five-out. Tried to make a concerted effort last game to get him in the post. Obviously, he’s gonna read and react. So a lot of the rip-screen stuff to get him to the block; if (defenders) go under (the screen), sometimes it leads to more side pick-and-roll where he picks and pops against the coverage. But would love to see him more down there at the block. Obviously, your post offense is dictated around the shooting that’s around him, so sometimes play calls or concepts, whatever you want to call it, it’s the four guys who are out there with him, too.” 
 Rookie forward Bryce Hopkins was another bright spot in Wednesday’s win. As Benedetto writes , the 49th overall pick in this year’s draft was unexpectedly inserted into the rotation with DeRozan ruled out and responded with a career-high 18 points on just seven field goal attempts to go along with four rebounds and two steals in 28 minutes. Both Adelman and Jokic praised Hopkins for his professional approach to the game. “ I feel like I’m just a very versatile player. I feel like I can create offense whether I’m off the ball or on the ball ,” Hopkins said. “ Whatever the team needs me to do, I feel like I can do it. I feel like my physicality is big for me on the defensive end and on the offensive end. Whatever the team needs me to do, I’m willing to do it .”
